rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Debt brings mental preoccupation, humiliation before creditors, and pressure that can lead to lying, broken promises, or broken oaths; these harms diminish its dignity.
rows.anchor:
الدين شين الدين "
وروي عنه أنه قال:
" الدين هم بالليل ومذلة بالنهار "
قال علماؤنا: وإنما كان شينا ومذلة لما فيه من شغل القلب والبال

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet sought refuge from sin and debt because indebted people may lie when speaking and break promises.
rows.anchor: إن الرجل إذا غرم حدث فكذب ووعد فأخلف

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A believer's soul remains pledged in the grave by an unpaid debt until someone pays it.
rows.anchor: نسمة المؤمن مرتهنة في قبره بدينه حتى يقضى عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commands to document, witness, and take pledges decisively require safeguarding and developing wealth, against ascetics who give everything away and leave dependants to others' charity or oppression.
rows.anchor: كان ذلك نصا قاطعا على مراعاة حفظ الأموال وتنميتها

rows.speaker: أبو الفرج الجوزي
rows.claim: Al-Jawzi condemns learned advocates of total divestment as opposing both reason and the law; he says al-Muhasibi and Abu Hamid al-Tusi reinforced that teaching.
rows.anchor: أتعجب من أقوام لهم علم وعقل كيف حثوا على هذا، وأمروا به مع مضادته للشرع والعقل

rows.speaker: المحاسبي
rows.claim: Al-Muhasibi recounts that some Companions feared for Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf because of his wealth, while Ka'b defended how he earned, spent, and left it.
rows.anchor: لما توفي عبد الرحمن بن عوف قال ناس من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: إنما نخاف على عبد الرحمن فيما ترك

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says the wealthy are few on Judgment Day, except those who give generously in both directions.
rows.anchor: الأكثرون هم الأقلون يوم القيامة إلا من قال هكذا وهكذا

rows.speaker: المحاسبي
rows.claim: Al-Muhasibi says Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf's lawful earnings delayed his entry with the poor, so he would crawl behind them toward Paradise.
rows.anchor: يوقف في عرصة يوم القيامة بسبب ما كسبه من حلال للتعفف وصنائع المعروف

rows.speaker: أبو حامد
rows.claim: Abu Hamid argues that even charitable wealth distracts from remembering God, so an aspirant should retain only necessities and give away every sum that occupies the heart.
rows.anchor: فما بقي له درهم يلتفت إليه قلبه فهو محجوب عن الله تعالى

rows.speaker: أبو الفرج الجوزي
rows.claim: Al-Jawzi answers that God dignified wealth as human sustenance, prohibited entrusting it to the foolish, and ordered its return when orphans attain sound judgment.
rows.anchor: وقد شرفه الله وعظم قدره وأمر بحفظه، إذ جعله قواما للآدمي وما جعل قواما للآدمي الشريف فهو شريف

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet told Sa'd that leaving heirs financially secure is better than leaving them needy and asking people for help.
rows.anchor: إنك أن تذر ورثتك أغنياء خير من أن تذرهم عالة يتكففون الناس

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet called sound wealth in the hands of a righteous person a good thing.
rows.anchor: نعم المال الصالح للرجل الصالح

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said Abu Bakr's wealth benefited him and prayed for Anas to receive abundant, blessed wealth and children.
rows.anchor: ما نفعني مال كمال أبي بكر

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When Ka'b offered to give away all his property as repentance, the Prophet told him to keep some because that was better.
rows.anchor: أمسك عليك بعض مالك فهو خير لك

rows.speaker: أبو الفرج الجوزي
rows.claim: Al-Jawzi acknowledges wealth's temptations but says lawful earnings are necessary; gathering more is judged by intent, and supporting one's family, poor people, and public good can make it better than many devotions.
rows.anchor: فإن قصد نفس المفاخرة والمباهاة فبئس المقصود، وإن قصد إعفاف نفسه وعائلته

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet allotted land to al-Zubayr according to how far his horse ran and his whip reached, an example of permitting acquisition.
rows.anchor: أقطع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم الزبير حضر فرسه أجرى الفرس حتى قام ثم رمي سوطه، فقال: «أعطوه حيث بلغ سوطه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Desire for increase is natural: Sa'd ibn Ubada prayed for abundance, Joseph's brothers sought an extra camel-load, Shu'ayb offered Moses ten years, and Job gathered golden locusts.
rows.anchor: وهذا أمر مركوز في الطباع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi calls al-Muhasibi's account of Abu Dharr confronting Ka'b impossible and fabricated; its claimed route through Ibn Lahi'a is unreliable, and Abu Dharr died seven years before Abd al-Rahman.
rows.anchor: والصحيح في التاريخ أن أبا ذر توفي سنة خمس وعشرين، وعبد الرحمن بن عوف توفي سنة اثنتين وثلاثين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story's content is implausible: the Companions would not condemn wealth lawfully acquired, and it makes no sense that the law would permit and then punish it.
rows.anchor: ثم كيف تقول الصحابة: إنا نخاف على عبد الرحمن! أو ليس الإجماع منعقدا على إباحة جمع المال من حله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The crawling report about Abd al-Rahman is weak: its transmitter Ammara ibn Zadhan was criticized by al-Bukhari, Ahmad, Abu Hatim, and al-Daraqutni.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حاتم الرازي: لا يحتج به، وقال الدارقطني: ضعيف

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib says wealth is needed to repay debts and protect one's honor; he left four hundred dinars, while Sufyan al-Thawri called money a weapon in that era.
rows.anchor: لا خير فيمن لا يطلب المال يقضي به دينه ويصون به عرضه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi says soundly intended accumulation of lawful wealth is better than abandoning it; early Muslims praised and gathered it for emergencies and helping the poor, while some chose less to focus on worship.
rows.anchor: ومتى صح القصد فجمعه أفضل بلا خلاف عند العلماء

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet's declaration that one killed defending property is a martyr is further evidence that wealth must be protected; fuller discussion is promised in al-Ma'ida.
rows.anchor:
من قتل دون ماله فهو شهيد "
وسيأتي بيانه في «المائدة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says whoever is killed defending his property is a martyr, showing that property deserves protection.
rows.anchor: من قتل دون ماله فهو شهيد

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A person from the People of Scripture who believed in his own prophet, then met Muhammad, believed and followed him, receives a double reward.
rows.anchor: رجل من أهل الكتاب آمن بنبيه ثم أدرك النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فآمن به واتبعه وصدقه فله أجران

rows.speaker: مجاهد وابن جريج وابن زيد
rows.claim: Mujahid, Ibn Jurayj, and Ibn Zayd say the verse was revealed about believers among the People of Scripture; it is general, with the Negus Ashama (Arabic: Atiyya) among them.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد وابن جريج وابن زيد نزلت في مؤمني أهل الكتاب، وهذا عام والنجاشي واحد منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word khashi'in means humble; grammatically it is a circumstantial accusative referring either to the pronoun in yu'min or to a pronoun in ilayhim or ilaykum.
rows.anchor: و { خاشعين } أذلة، ونصب على الحال من المضمر الذي في «يؤمن».

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing verse gathers ten exhortations and promises worldly victory over enemies and success in the afterlife; patience is required in obedience and against desires.
rows.anchor: ختم تعالى السورة بما تضمنته هذه الآية العاشرة من الوصاة التي جمعت الظهور في الدنيا على الأعداء والفوز بنعيم الآخرة

rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam interprets sabiru as steadfastness against enemies.
rows.anchor: معناه مصابرة الأعداء قاله زيد بن أسلم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan interprets sabiru as persevering in the five daily prayers.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: على الصلوات الخمس

rows.speaker: عطاء والقرظي
rows.claim: Ata and al-Qurazi interpret sabiru as patiently awaiting God's promised relief without despair; Abu Umar chooses this view, though the enemy-facing interpretation is the majority view.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء والقرظي: صابروا الوعد الذي وعدتم. أي لا تيأسوا وانتظروا الفرج

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says waiting patiently for relief is an act of worship.
rows.anchor: انتظار الفرج بالصبر عبادة

rows.speaker: عنترة
rows.claim: Antara's verse illustrates sabiru as standing firm against an enemy in battle without cowardice; mukafaha denotes facing and confronting in combat.
rows.anchor:
فلم أر حيا صابروا مثل صبرنا
ولا كافحوا مثل الذين نكافح

rows.speaker: جمهور الأمة
rows.claim: The majority interpret rabitu as stationing and tethering horses to face the enemy, as the Quran elsewhere mentions tethered war-horses.
rows.anchor: فقال جمهور الأمة: رابطوا أعداءكم بالخيل، أي ارتبطواها كما يرتبطها أعداءكم

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: In a letter to Abu Ubayda about Roman forces, Umar says hardship is followed by relief, one hardship will not defeat two eases, and cites this verse.
rows.anchor: كتب أبو عبيدة بن الجراح إلى عمر بن الخطاب يذكر له جموعا من الروم وما يتخوف منهم

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy ibn Ka'b reports that a day of ribat outside Ramadan earns more than a century of fasting and prayer; during Ramadan it earns more than a millennium, and the reward continues after safe return.
rows.anchor: لرباط يوم في سبيل الله من وراء عورة المسلمين محتسبا من غير شهر رمضان أعظم أجرا من عبادة مائة سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi infers that a day of Ramadan ribat brings enduring reward even if the person returns safely rather than dying on duty.
rows.anchor: ودل هذا الحديث على أن رباط يوم في شهر رمضان يحصل له من الثواب الدائم وإن لم يمت مرابطا

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Anas reports that one night guarding in God's path exceeds a thousand years of fasting and night prayer at home, with each year counted as 360 days and each day as a thousand years.
rows.anchor: حرس ليلة في سبيل الله أفضل من صيام رجل وقيامه في أهله ألف سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because waiting for one prayer after another is also called ribat, those waiting for prayers may receive this merit, God willing.
rows.anchor: وجاء في انتظار الصلاة بعد الصلاة أنه رباط فقد يحصل لمنتظر الصلوات ذلك الفضل

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
rows.claim: The Prophet praised Muslims who completed Maghrib and awaited Isha, saying God opened heaven and boasted of them to the angels.
rows.anchor: قضوا فريضة وهم ينتظرون أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taqwa means the believers were not commanded to fight without piety; la'allakum may express hope or purpose, and falah means enduring success, points discussed fully in al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: واتقوا الله } أي لم تؤمروا بالجهاد من غير تقوى. { لعلكم تفلحون } لتكونوا على رجاء من الفلاح

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet told Hind to take enough customary support for herself and her child; another report about a son asking to be fed indicates this applies to one unable to earn.
rows.anchor: خذي ما يكفيك وولدك بالمعروف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Someone who has reached puberty is expected to seek a livelihood, since the verse sets reaching marriageable age as a threshold.
rows.anchor: ومن بلغ سن الحلم فلا يقول ذلك لأنه قد بلغ حد السعي على نفسه والكسب لها

rows.speaker: عطاء والزهري
rows.claim: Ata, al-Zuhri, and Kufan jurists say a wife cannot seek separation for her husband's poverty and should await payment as a court debt; they cite the respite for an insolvent debtor and the encouragement to marry the poor.
rows.anchor:
هذا قول عطاء والزهري. وإليه ذهب الكوفيون متمسكين بقوله تعالى:
وإن كان ذو عسرة فنظرة إلى ميسرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi says the cited verses do not prove that position, while the report about the wife demanding support or divorce directly addresses the dispute.
rows.anchor: ولا حجة لهم في هذه الآية على ما يأتي بيانه في موضعها. والحديث نص في موضع الخلاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative takes the address as directed to the orphan's guardian, who should spend according to the child's means and needs; if the child has no property, the state and then closest Muslims, especially the mother, must care for him without reimbursement.
rows.anchor: فالوصي ينفق على اليتيم على قدر ماله وحاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Speaking kindly means gentle address and reassuring promises; interpretations include prayers for the child and promising delivery of the estate once he is prudent.
rows.anchor: أراد تليين الخطاب والوعد الجميل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to test orphans addresses everyone and explains how their property is to be delivered; one occasion reported is the uncle of the orphaned Thabit ibn Rifa'a asking the Prophet what he may use and when to return the child's assets.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنها نزلت في ثابت بن رفاعة وفي عمه. وذلك أن رفاعة توفي وترك ابنه وهو صغير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Testing means assessing character, judgment, and ability to manage property; a promising child may receive a small trial amount, with the full estate delivered if managed well and retained if mismanaged.
rows.anchor: فإذا توسم الخير قال علماؤنا وغيرهم: لا بأس أن يدفع إليه شيئا من ماله يبيح له التصرف فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Passing a test alone does not end guardianship: the verse also requires reaching marriageable age before the estate is released.
rows.anchor: وليس في العلماء من يقول: إنه إذا اختبر الصبي فوجده رشيدا ترتفع الولاية عنه

rows.speaker: جماعة من الفقهاء
rows.claim: Some jurists test a boy by letting him manage household expenses for a month or a small sum under supervision; if he shows sound judgment, the guardian hands over the estate and witnesses it.
rows.anchor: وقال جماعة من الفقهاء: الصغير لا يخلو من أحد أمرين إما أن يكون غلاما أو جارية

rows.speaker: جماعة من الفقهاء
rows.claim: For a girl, some jurists test household management, such as supervising cotton workers and judging the yarn; if prudent, her estate is delivered with witnesses, otherwise guardianship continues.
rows.anchor: وإن كانت جارية رد إليها ما يرد إلى ربة البيت من تدبير بيتها والنظر فيه

rows.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد وغيرهما
rows.claim: Hasan, Mujahid, and others say orphans should be tested in intellect, religion, and the growth of their assets.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن ومجاهد وغيرهما: اختبروهم في عقولهم وأديانهم وتنمية أموالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reaching marriageable age means puberty, as shown by the Quran's parallel phrase about children reaching puberty; puberty can be established by five signs, three shared by both sexes and menstruation and pregnancy specific to women.
rows.anchor: وإذا بلغ الأطفال منكم الحلم

rows.speaker: العلماء
rows.claim: Scholars agree menstruation and pregnancy establish female puberty and trigger legal duties and rulings.
rows.anchor: فأما الحيض والحبل فلم يختلف العلماء في أنه بلوغ، وأن الفرائض والأحكام تجب بهما

rows.speaker: الأوزاعي والشافعي وابن حنبل
rows.claim: Al-Awza'i, al-Shafi'i, and Ibn Hanbal, with several Medinese authorities, set puberty at fifteen for someone without a wet dream; legal duties and penalties then apply, and Ibn al-Arabi prefers this limit.
rows.anchor: قال الأوزاعي والشافعي وابن حنبل: خمس عشرة سنة بلوغ لمن لم يحتلم

rows.speaker: أصبغ بن الفرج
rows.claim: Asbagh says fifteen is the best legal threshold because it is also the age at which a boy receives a share in military service and is allowed into battle.
rows.anchor: إن حد البلوغ الذي تلزم به الفرائض والحدود خمس عشرة سنة

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar's report supports fifteen as an age threshold: the Prophet accepted him for the Trench at fifteen but had rejected him at Uhud at fourteen.
rows.anchor: إذ عرض يوم الخندق وهو ابن خمس عشرة سنة فأجيز، ولم يجز يوم أحد لأنه كان ابن أربع عشرة سنة

rows.speaker: أبو عمر بن عبد البر
rows.claim: For people whose birth dates are unknown, Ibn Abd al-Barr reports Umar's instruction to assess puberty by the appearance of pubic hair; Uthman used a similar sign when judging a boy who stole.
rows.anchor: هذا فيمن عرف مولده، وأما من جهل مولده وعدة سنه أو جحده فالعمل فيه بما روى نافع عن أسلم عن عمر

rows.speaker: عطية القرظي
rows.claim: Atiyya al-Qurazi says the Prophet inspected Banu Qurayza after Sa'd ibn Mu'adh's ruling, killing those who had grown pubic hair and sparing those who had not; he was spared.
rows.anchor: عرض رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بني قريظة فكل من أنبت منهم قتله بحكم سعد بن معاذ

rows.speaker: مالك وأبو حنيفة وغيرهما
rows.claim: Malik, Abu Hanifa, and others set maturity by puberty rather than age; the text gives seventeen years, while Malik also cited a deepened voice and altered nostrils, and Abu Hanifa's best-known view is nineteen for boys and seventeen for girls.
rows.anchor: وقال مالك وأبو حنيفة وغيرهما: لا يحكم لمن لم يحتلم حتى يبلغ ما لم يبلغه أحد إلا احتلم، وذلك سبع عشرة سنة

rows.speaker: داود
rows.claim: Dawud says age never establishes puberty without a wet dream, even if someone reaches forty.
rows.anchor: وقال داود: لا يبلغ بالسن ما لم يحتلم ولو بلغ أربعين سنة

rows.speaker: ابن القاسم وسالم
rows.claim: Ibn al-Qasim, Salim, and several jurists treat pubic hair as a sign of puberty; another Shafi'i view uses that sign specifically in the Banu Qurayza ruling, while green stubble is not enough.
rows.anchor: فأما الإنبات فمنهم من قال: يستدل به على البلوغ روي عن ابن القاسم وسالم

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik says his operative practice follows Umar's report: someone on whom the razor passes is legally mature for punishment.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن القاسم: سمعت مالكا يقول: العمل عندي على حديث عمربن الخطاب

rows.speaker: أصبغ
rows.claim: Asbagh prefers imposing a penalty only when both pubic hair and puberty are established.
rows.anchor: وأحب إلي ألا يقام عليه الحد إلا باجتماع الإنبات والبلوغ

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa rejects pubic hair as either proof or indication of puberty.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة: لا يثبت بالإنبات حكم، وليس هو ببلوغ ولا دلالة على البلوغ

rows.speaker: الزهري وعطاء
rows.claim: Al-Zuhri, Ata, al-Shafi'i, and some Malikis say no penalty applies before a wet dream, apparently assigning no legal force to age or pubic hair.
rows.anchor: وقال الزهري وعطاء: لا حد على من لم يحتلم وهو قول الشافعي

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi argues that if the Prophet's fifteen-year ruling is not evidence, other proposed ages are unsupported; jurists should use both age and pubic hair, which the Prophet explicitly recognized.
rows.anchor: إذا لم يكن حديث ابن عمر دليلا في السن فكل عدد يذكرونه من السنين فإنه دعوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi notes that Ibn al-Arabi took the opposite position in al-Anfal, reading Ibn Umar's report as distinguishing those able to fight and receive spoils from dependants; Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz understood it similarly.
rows.anchor: هذا قوله هنا، وقال في سورة الأنفال عكسه إذ لم يعرج على حديث ابن عمر هناك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anistu means perceived or saw, as in Moses seeing a fire; al-Azhari explains the idiom as looking to see whether anyone is there, and al-Nabigha's wild bull poem illustrates watchful looking.
rows.anchor:
أي أبصرتم ورأيتم ومنه قوله تعالى
آنس من جانب الطور نارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb can also mean sensed, found, or knew; its underlying sense is seeing.
rows.anchor: وقيل: آنست وأحسست ووجدت بمعنى واحد ومنه قوله تعالى: { فإن آنستم منهم رشدا } أي علمتم

rows.speaker: السلمي وعيسى والثقفي وابن مسعود
rows.claim: The common reading has rushdan with a damma on ra and silent shin; al-Sulami, Isa, al-Thaqafi, and Ibn Masud read it with both vowels open, two dialectal forms and possible verbal nouns.
rows.anchor: وقراءة العامة «رشدا» بضم الراء وسكون الشين. وقرأ السلمي وعيسى والثقفي وابن مسعود رضي الله عنهم «رشدا» بفتح الراء والشين

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وغيرهما
rows.claim: Hasan, Qatada, and others interpret rushd as soundness of intellect and religion.
rows.anchor: فقال الحسن وقتادة وغيرهما: صلاحا في العقل والدين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي والثوري
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Suddi, and al-Thawri define sound judgment as competence of mind and preservation of wealth.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس والسدي والثوري: صلاحا في العقل وحفظ المال

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير والشعبي
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Sha'bi say even an old person should not receive an orphan's estate until prudence is observed; al-Dahhak likewise withholds it even at a hundred absent sound management.
rows.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير والشعبي: إن الرجل ليأخذ بلحيته وما بلغ رشده فلا يدفع إلى اليتيم ماله

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says rushd refers specifically to intellect.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: «رشدا» يعني في العقل خاصة

rows.speaker: أكثر العلماء
rows.claim: Most scholars, including Malik, say sound judgment follows puberty; a person who remains imprudent stays under guardianship even when old.
rows.anchor: وأكثر العلماء على أن الرشد لا يكون إلا بعد البلوغ

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة وزفر بن الهذيل والنخعي
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa, Zufar, and al-Nakha'i say a free adult cannot be placed under guardianship once he reaches manhood, even if profligate, so long as he is rational.
rows.anchor: لا يحجر على الحر البالغ إذا بلغ مبلغ الرجال، ولو كان أفسق الناس وأشدهم تبذيرا

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada transmits the case of Habban ibn Munqidh, whose weak commercial judgment prompted a request for interdiction; the Prophet instead told him to state that there was no fraud and that he had three days to withdraw.
rows.anchor: أن حبان بن منقذ كان يبتاع وفي عقدته ضعف، فقيل: يا رسول الله احجر عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The case does not prove that guardianship is forbidden, because it was specific to Habban, as al-Qurtubi explained under al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: وهذا لا حجة لهم فيه لأنه مخصوص بذلك على ما بيناه في البقرة

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafi'i interdicts someone who corrupts both wealth and religion or wealth alone; if religion is corrupt but wealth managed, one view interdicts him and another does not.
rows.anchor: إن كان مفسدا لماله ودينه، أو كان مفسدا لماله دون دينه حجر عليه

rows.speaker: أبو العباس بن شريح
rows.claim: Ibn Shurayh chooses the Shafi'i view that a person who misuses religion but manages wealth should still be interdicted.
rows.anchor: أحدهما يحجر عليه وهو اختيار أبي العباس بن شريح

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق المروزي
rows.claim: Al-Maruzi chooses not to interdict someone who is religiously corrupt but manages wealth; al-Qurtubi calls this the apparent Shafi'i position.
rows.anchor: والثاني لا حجر عليه وهو اختيار أبي إسحاق المروزي، والأظهر من مذهب الشافعي

rows.speaker: الثعلبي
rows.claim: Al-Tha'labi attributes the permissibility of interdicting a spendthrift to Uthman, Ali, al-Zubayr, Aisha, Ibn Abbas, Abd Allah ibn Ja'far, Shurayh, and many jurists, and reports a claim of consensus.
rows.anchor: وهذا الذي ذكرناه من الحجر على السفيه قول عثمان وعلي والزبير وعائشة وابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Property is delivered only when both sound judgment and puberty are present; most jurists agree, while Abu Hanifa, Zufar, and al-Nakha'i release a person at twenty-five without requiring sound judgment.
rows.anchor:
دفع المال يكون بشرطين: إيناس الرشد
 والبلوغ، فإن وجد أحدهما دون الآخر لم يجز تسليم المال

rows.speaker: علماؤنا
rows.claim: Maliki scholars require a girl to have consummated marriage after puberty before testing her judgment, reasoning that seclusion limits her experience; men encounter public dealings from childhood.
rows.anchor: إلا أن علماءنا شرطوا في الجارية دخول الزوج بها مع البلوغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi prefers al-Shafi'i's view that intercourse itself adds nothing to a woman's judgment if she already understands affairs and manages her wealth.
rows.anchor: وما قاله الشافعي أصوب فإن نفس الوطء بإدخال الحشفة لا يزيدها في رشدها

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi reports Maliki waiting periods of five to seven years for a girl with a father and one year for an orphan, but says these limits lack evidence and are difficult to define; the Quranic criterion is demonstrated judgment suited to each person.
rows.anchor: وليس في هذا كله دليل، وتحديد الأعوام في ذات الأب عسير وأعسر منه تحديد العام في اليتيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi criticizes Abu Hanifa's grandfather rationale and Abu Bakr al-Razi's argument from two verses: unrestricted wording must, by agreement among legal theorists, be read with the qualified wording.
rows.anchor: فإن هذا من باب المطلق والمقيد، والمطلق يرد إلى المقيد باتفاق أهل الأصول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once a girl is prudent, contracts made during the waiting period are treated either as void until then or as valid only when sound judgment is shown; after it, they are accepted unless folly appears.
rows.anchor: واختلفوا فيما فعلته ذات الأب في تلك المدة فقيل: هو محمول على الرد لبقاء الحجر

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Views differ on whether a guardian must obtain a judge's confirmation before release; Ibn Atiyya says guardians today should, given collusion and false declarations of a ward's prudence.
rows.anchor: والصواب في أوصياء زماننا ألا يستغني عن رفعه إلى السلطان وثبوت الرشد عنده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Malik and one Shafi'i view restore guardianship if a released person becomes wasteful; Abu Hanifa says it cannot return, but al-Qurtubi cites the Quran's protection of wealth and its provision for a guardian when a debtor becomes foolish or weak.
rows.anchor: ثم عاد إلى السفه بظهور تبذير وقلة تدبير عاد إليه الحجر عندنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A guardian may manage an orphan's estate as a father would: trade, pay zakat and obligations, cover damages and parents' support, arrange marriage, pay a dowry, acquire a concubine, and settle claims in the ward's interest.
rows.anchor: ويجوز للوصي أن يصنع في مال اليتيم ما كان للأب أن يصنعه من تجارة وإبضاع وشراء وبيع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A guardian who pays some creditors from an estate is not liable if funds sufficient for the remaining debts are later lost; if he knowingly distributes the whole estate despite other debts, he must make up the other creditors' shares.
rows.anchor: فإن كان عالما بالدين الباقي أو كان الميت معروفا بالدين الباقي ضمن الوصي لهؤلاء الغرماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A guardian who pays a deceased person's debt without witnesses is liable; if payment was witnessed but the witnesses later die after a long time, he is not liable.
rows.anchor: وإذا دفع الوصي دين الميت بغير إشهاد ضمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi points back to al-Baqara 2:220 for fuller rulings on guardians' spending and other fiduciary duties.
rows.anchor: من أحكام الوصي في الإنفاق وغيره ما فيه كفاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition does not imply that non-extravagant consumption is allowed; it forbids consuming the orphan's property except what is specifically permitted. Israf means excess or transgression.
rows.anchor: ليس يريد أن أكل ما لهم من غير إسراف جائز، فيكون له دليل خطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Arabic word israf is explained as excess, crossing a limit, erroneous spending, waste, or heedlessness; poems illustrate the word's usage.
rows.anchor: والإسراف في اللغة الإفراط ومجاوزة الحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Badaran means rushing to consume before an orphan reaches maturity; grammatically it is coordinated with israfan, and an yakbaru is governed by badaran.
rows.anchor: وهو معطوف على «إسرافا» و { أن يكبروا } في موضع نصب ب «بدارا»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A wealthy guardian must refrain from the orphan's funds, while a poor guardian may consume customary support; isti'faf means abstaining, as in the command to unmarried people.
rows.anchor:
والاستعفاف عن الشيء تركه. ومنه قوله تعالى:
وليستعفف الذين لا يجدون نكاحا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A poor guardian who has an orphan may consume from the child's assets only without excess, waste, or accumulating principal.
rows.anchor: كل من مال يتيمك غير مسرف ولا مباذر ولا متأثل

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha says the allowance applies to a needy guardian who cares for and improves the orphan's affairs; one narration limits it proportionately to the estate.
rows.anchor: نزلت في ولي اليتيم الذي يقوم عليه ويصلحه إذا كان محتاجا جاز أن يأكل منه

rows.speaker: ربيعة ويحيى بن سعيد
rows.claim: Rabi'a and Yahya ibn Sa'id instead take the verse to mean that the orphan receives support according to whether his own assets are ample or limited; al-Qurtubi says the majority view is correct because the child cannot manage his money.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم: المراد اليتيم إن كان غنيا وسع عليه وأعف عن ماله، وإن كان فقيرا أنفق عليه بقدره

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب وابن عباس وعبيدة وابن جبير والشعبي ومجاهد وأبو العالية
rows.claim: One view lets an impoverished guardian borrow customary support and repay it when solvent; Umar compared his use of public funds to a guardian's use of an orphan's property.
rows.anchor: فقال قوم: هو القرض إذا احتاج ويقضي إذا أيسر، قاله عمربن الخطاب

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abu al-Aliya explicitly interprets customary consumption as a loan, citing the command to witness the return of the assets.
rows.anchor: ومن كان فقيرا فليأكل بالمعروف } قال: قرضا ثم تلا { فإذا دفعتم إليهم أموالهم فأشهدوا عليهم

rows.speaker: إبراهيم وعطاء والحسن البصري والنخعي وقتادة
rows.claim: A second view says a poor guardian owes no repayment because modest food and clothing are compensation from God for responsible care; luxury clothing is excluded, and the jurists support it by analogy to an imam's stipend.
rows.anchor: لا قضاء على الوصي الفقير فيما يأكل بالمعروف لأن ذلك حق النظر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وأبو العالية والشعبي
rows.claim: Another explanation allows use of an orphan's livestock milk, servants, or animals so long as the estate is not harmed; jurists compare this to fair wages, with any excess forbidden.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس وأبي العالية والشعبي أن الأكل بالمعروف هو كالانتفاع بألبان المواشي، واستخدام العبيد، وركوب الدواب

rows.speaker: الحسن بن صالح بن حي
rows.claim: Hasan ibn Salih distinguishes the father's appointed guardian, who may take customary support, from a judge's guardian, who may take nothing.
rows.anchor: فرق الحسن بن صالح بن حي ويقال ابن حيان بين وصي الأب والحاكم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the allowance is abrogated by the prohibition on consuming wealth without trade by mutual consent, because guardianship is not a sale.
rows.anchor: روى عن مجاهد قال: ليس له أن يأخذ قرضا ولا غيره

rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says the allowance is abrogated by the warning against consuming orphan property unjustly.
rows.anchor:
وقال زيد بن أسلم: إن الرخصة في هذه الآية منسوخة بقوله تعالى:
إن الذين يأكلون أموال اليتامى ظلما

rows.speaker: أبو يوسف
rows.claim: Abu Yusuf says he is unsure whether the allowance was abrogated by the prohibition on consuming wealth without consensual trade.
rows.anchor: وحكى بشر بن الوليد عن أبي يوسف قال: لا أدري، لعل هذه الآية منسوخة

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأبو يوسف ومحمد
rows.claim: A fifth view bars taking from the orphan's principal while the guardian remains at home, but permits necessary expenses when traveling for the orphan, without acquiring property.
rows.anchor: وقول خامس وهو الفرق بين الحضر والسفر فيمنع إذا كان مقيما معه في المصر

rows.speaker: أبو قلابة
rows.claim: Abu Qilaba permits consuming from the orphan's profits but not taking liquid capital as a loan or otherwise.
rows.anchor: فليأكل بالمعروف مما يجني من الغلة فأما المال الناض فليس له أن يأخذ منه شيئا

rows.speaker: عكرمة عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas through Ikrima limits the allowance to a guardian who is in need and desperate.
rows.anchor: روى عكرمة عن ابن عباس { ومن كان فقيرا فليأكل بالمعروف } قال: إذا احتاج واضطر

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Sha'bi compares the guardian's need to necessity for carrion or pork, permitting a limited taking and repayment if able; al-Nahhas says actual necessity already allows taking enough from any available source.
rows.anchor: وقال الشعبي: كذلك إذا كان منه بمنزلة الدم ولحم الخنزير أخذ منه فإن وجد أوفى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والنخعي
rows.claim: Another Ibn Abbas and al-Nakha'i interpretation tells guardians to live modestly from their own funds so they will not need the orphan's money; al-Nahhas calls this the strongest report because others' property is inviolable without clear proof.
rows.anchor: المراد أن يأكل الوصي بالمعروف من مال نفسه حتى لا يحتاج إلى مال اليتيم

rows.speaker: الكيا الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Kiya al-Tabari agrees that the verse requires subsistence from one's own property, not the child's; he harmonizes its ambiguity with clear prohibitions on consuming another's wealth without consent, especially an orphan's.
rows.anchor: توهم متوهمون من السلف بحكم الآية أن للوصي أن يأكل من مال الصبي

rows.speaker: الكيا الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Kiya answers that judges' salaries come from unowned public funds, whereas a guardian would take from a specific owner without consent for undefined work and an undefined wage.
rows.anchor: والوصي إنما يأخذ بعمله مال شخص معين من غير رضاه وعمله مجهول وأجرته مجهولة

rows.speaker: أبو العباس
rows.claim: Abu al-Abbas allows fair compensation when a large estate demands substantial work; for a trivial estate he permits only customary small quantities of milk, food, or ghee without harm or excess.
rows.anchor: إن كان مال اليتيم كثيرا يحتاج إلى كبير قيام عليه بحيث يشغل الولي عن حاجاته ومهماته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi says abstaining from compensation is better; he condemns fees taken by partition judges and their agents as unlawful and within the threat against consuming orphan property.
rows.anchor: قلت: والاحتراز عنه أفضل، إن شاء الله. وأما ما يأخذه قاضي القسمة ويسميه رسما ونهب أتباعه فلا أدري له وجها ولا حلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Witnessing the handover is commanded to secure the assets and clear suspicion; scholars differ whether it is recommended, since a guardian is trusted, or obligatory, since he cannot testify in his own favor against heirs.
rows.anchor: أمر الله تعالى بالإشهاد تنبيها على التحصين وزوالا للتهم

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب وابن جبير
rows.claim: Umar and Ibn Jubayr understand the witnesses to document repayment by a poor guardian of a loan from the orphan's assets.
rows.anchor: ورأى عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه وابن جبير أن هذا الإشهاد إنما هو على دفع الوصي

rows.speaker: عبيدة
rows.claim: Ubayda says the verse proves that a guardian who borrowed or consumed the orphan's assets must witness repayment once solvent.
rows.anchor: قال عبيدة هذه الآية دليل على وجوب القضاء على من أكل المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi says the wording covers both repayment and any spending for a ward; witnessing is the apparent command, and a witnessed entrustment is discharged only by witnessed return.
rows.anchor: والصحيح أن اللفظ يعم هذا وسواه. والظاهر أن المراد إذا أنفقتم شيئا على المولى عليه فأشهدوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guardian must also protect the orphan's body through discipline and care, just as he safeguards and develops the child's assets; al-Qurtubi discussed this in al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: كما على الوصي والكفيل حفظ مال يتيمه والتثمير له، كذلك عليه حفظ الصبي في بدنه

rows.speaker: رجل قال للنبي
rows.claim: A man asks whether he may consume an orphan's assets and discipline him; the Prophet allows modest use without accumulating wealth or shielding his own assets, and says to discipline the child as one would one's own.
rows.anchor: وروي أن رجلا قال للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: إن في حجري يتيما

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says that although the report is not established with a connected chain, no one can find a way to avoid its ruling.
rows.anchor: وإن لم يثبت مسندا فليس يجد أحد عنه ملتحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is sufficient as accountant of deeds and their recompense, a warning to everyone who denies a right; grammatically the b in billahi is additional and the subject is nominative.
rows.anchor: أي كفى الله حاسبا لأعمالكم ومجازيا بها. ففي هذا وعيد لكل جاحد حق

rows.speaker: القفال وغيره
rows.claim: Al-Qaffal and others interpret meeting God as meeting the resurrection and its recompense, citing the threat against one who swears falsely to take a Muslim's property.
rows.anchor:
قيل: بالبعث بعد الموت وبالجزاء دليله قوله عليه السلام:
" من حلف على يمين كاذبة

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayri rejects that interpretation: using meeting to mean recompense where context requires it does not justify doing so here; the phrase should retain its literal sense, since deniers of God and of vision deny existence.
rows.anchor: وهذا ليس بشيء لأن حمل اللقاء في موضع على الجزاء لدليل قائم لا يوجب هذا التأويل في كل موضع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hour is named for the rapid reckoning that occurs then; baghtatan means suddenly and is a circumstantial accusative, a verbal noun used as a state according to Sibawayh.
rows.anchor: سميت القيامة بالساعة لسرعة الحساب فيها. ومعنى «بغتة» فجأة

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh treats baghtatan as a verbal noun in the accusative of state, like qataltuhu sabran, but does not allow extending the pattern by analogy to saying someone came quickly.
rows.anchor: وهي عند سيبويه مصدر في موضع الحال، كما تقول: قتلته صبرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling out to regret is not literal address: it intensifies sorrow, like calling on wonder; Sibawayh imagines summoning sorrow to arrive, stronger than simply saying one is amazed.
rows.anchor: وقع النداء على الحسرة وليست بمنادى في الحقيقة، ولكنه يدل على كثرة التحسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation treats the cry as a warning to people about the immense regret coming upon them, using an apparent addressee who is not literally being addressed.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو تنبيه للناس على عظيم ما يحل بهم من الحسرة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says the neglected preparation was for the Hour itself.
rows.anchor: على ما فرطنا فيها } أي في الساعة، أي في التقدمة لها عن الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Farratna means we neglected or squandered; its root evokes going ahead, so the phrase may mean letting others precede us in obedience or failing to act for the Hour in worldly life.
rows.anchor: معناه ضيعنا وأصله التقدم يقال

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari takes the pronoun to refer to a transaction: they regret trading faith for disbelief and the afterlife for worldly life, as the loss-of-trade wording in al-Baqara indicates.
rows.anchor: وقال الطبري: الهاء راجعة إلى الصفقة، وذلك أنهم لما تبين لهم خسران صفقتهم

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says their regret concerns neglecting deeds that would lead to Paradise.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: على ما ضيعنا أي من عمل الجنة

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: A report from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri says the people of Hell see their homes in Paradise and cry out in regret.
rows.anchor: يرى أهل النار منازلهم في الجنة فيقولون: «يا حسرتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their burdens are sins, described metaphorically as physical loads on their backs; wizr originates from the idea of a mountain or weight and also appears in the funeral phrase about returning burdened, not rewarded.
rows.anchor: أي ذنوبهم جمع وزر. { على ظهورهم } مجاز وتوسع وتشبيه بمن يحمل ثقلا

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: Abu Ubayd says the funeral phrase should be mawzurat, burdened with sin, rather than the common ma'zurat, because the root is wizr.
rows.anchor: والعامة تقول: «مأزورات» كأنه لا وجه له عنده لأنه من الوزر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wazir derives from carrying the burdens of governance; the verse means sins cling to the disbelievers and weigh them down, and the final clause calls their burden vile.
rows.anchor: والمعنى أنهم لزمتهم الآثام فصاروا مثقلين بها

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: Nafi' reads the n in a-tuhajjooni with light pronunciation; the other readers double it, though a variant is reported from Ibn Amir through Hisham.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع بتخفيف النون، وشدد النون الباقون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The doubled form contracts two original nuns, the nominative marker and a separator before ya; the light form drops the second nun to avoid duplication while retaining the grammatical marker.
rows.anchor: الأصل فيه نونان، الأولى علامة الرفع والثانية فاصلة بين الفعل والياء

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
rows.claim: Abu Amr calls the light reading ungrammatical, but Sibawayh permits it because doubled consonants are burdensome and cites a line of poetry.
rows.anchor: وحكي عن أبي عمرو بن العلاء أن هذه القراءة لحن. وأجاز سيبويه ذلك فقال: استثقلوا التضعيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham does not fear the idols because they cannot benefit or harm him, despite his people threatening him with their many gods; harm could occur only if God willed it for a sin.
rows.anchor: ولا أخاف ما تشركون به } أي لأنه لا ينفع ولا يضر وكانوا خوفوه بكثرة آلهتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception is not from the preceding fear: God may decree some hardship for a sin; the pronoun in bihi may refer either to God or to the idol.
rows.anchor: وهذا استثناء ليس من الأول. والهاء في «به» يحتمل أن تكون لله عز وجل، ويجوز أن تكون للمعبود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's phrase also means that God does not will him to fear the idols; God's knowledge encompasses everything.
rows.anchor: يعني أن الله تعالى لا يشاء أن أخافهم. ثم قال: { وسع ربي كل شيء علما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question how Abraham could fear what they associate with God is a rebuke: idols are lifeless, while they do not fear the omnipotent God.
rows.anchor: ففي «كيف» معنى الإنكار أنكر عليهم تخويفهم إياه بالأصنام وهم لا يخافون الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A deity without revealed authority means an idol without proof or warrant.
rows.anchor: ما لم ينزل به عليكم سلطانا } أي حجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two parties in the security contest are the monotheist and the polytheist, and security means safety from God's punishment.
rows.anchor: فأي الفريقين أحق بالأمن } أي من عذاب الله: الموحد أم المشرك

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق وعلي وسلمان وحذيفة
rows.claim: Abu Bakr, Ali, Salman, and Hudhayfa interpret the wrong that faith must not be mixed with as shirk.
rows.anchor: الذين آمنوا ولم يلبسوا إيمانهم بظلم } أي بشرك قاله أبو بكر الصديق وعلي وسلمان وحذيفة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the words are Abraham's own answer, as when a teacher asks and answers his own question.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: هو من قول إبراهيم كما يسأل العالم ويجيب نفسه

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj says Abraham's people said the words, giving an answer that became evidence against them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو من قول قوم إبراهيم أي أجابوا بما هو حجة عليهم قاله ابن جريج

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When the Companions feared that every wrong disqualified them, the Prophet explained the verse by citing Luqman's statement that associating partners with God is grave injustice.
rows.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: ليس هو كما تظنون إنما هو كما قال لقمان لابنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being guided refers to guidance in this worldly life.
rows.anchor: وهم مهتدون } أي في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Come means come forward and hear a certain, true recitation revealed by God, not conjecture or falsehood as the opponents alleged.
rows.anchor: أي تقدموا واقرءوا حقا يقينا كما أوحى إلي ربي، لا ظنا ولا كذبا

rows.speaker: ابن الشجري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Shajari explains the forms of ta'ala for singulars and groups; the word first meant rise and come forward, then broadened to include someone already standing or walking.
rows.anchor: وجعلوا التقدم ضربا من التعالي والارتفاع لأن المأمور بالتقدم في أصل وضع هذا الفعل

rows.speaker: البصريون
rows.claim: The Basran analysis attaches alaykum to the nearer verb harama, making ma the object of atlu; the Kufan analysis attaches it to the earlier atlu.
rows.anchor: فإن علقت «عليكم» ب «حرم» فهو الوجه لأنه الأقرب وهو اختيار البصريين

rows.speaker: ابن الشجري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Shajari analyzes alla tushriku as an accusative after an implied repeated verb, or as an exhortation in which alaykum stands independently; al-Nahhas offers apposition to ma, while al-Farra takes la as prohibition.
rows.anchor: ألا تشركوا } في موضع نصب بتقدير فعل من لفظ الأول، أي أتل عليكم ألا تشركوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse commands the Prophet to summon all people to hear God's prohibitions; later scholars must likewise teach people what is forbidden and lawful.
rows.anchor: هذه الآية أمر من الله تعالى لنبيه عليه السلام بأن يدعو جميع الخلق إلى سماع تلاوة ما حرم الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The obligation to explain prohibitions is reinforced by the command that scripture be made clear to people rather than concealed.
rows.anchor: لتبيننه للناس ولا تكتمونه

rows.speaker: ربيع بن خيثم
rows.claim: Ibn al-Mubarak reports Rabi ibn Khuthaym asking a companion if he would like a sealed letter from the Prophet; he then reads this verse through the end of the three verses.
rows.anchor: قال ربيع بن خيثم لجليس له: أيسرك أن تؤتى بصحيفة

rows.speaker: كعب الأحبار
rows.claim: Ka'b al-Ahbar says this passage opens the Torah.
rows.anchor: وقال كعب الأحبار: هذه الآية مفتتح التوراة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says these are the decisive verses mentioned in Aal Imran, agreed upon by revealed laws and never abrogated; another view identifies them as the Ten Commandments given to Moses.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: هذه الآيات المحكمات التي ذكرها الله في سورة «آل عمران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ihsan to parents entails honoring, caring for, protecting, obeying, freeing them from bondage, and not exercising domination over them; grammatically ihsanan is an accusative verbal noun with an implied command.
rows.anchor: الإحسان إلى الوالدين برهما وحفظهما وصيانتهما وامتثال أمرهما وإزالة الرق عنهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Imلاق means poverty: do not bury daughters or kill children out of fear of hardship, because God provides for parents and children; some also killed boys and girls from poverty.
rows.anchor: الإملاق الفقر: أي لا تئدوا من الموءودة بناتكم خشية العيلة، فإني رازقكم وإياهم

rows.speaker: مؤرج
rows.claim: Mu'rij says imlaq means hunger in the language of Lakhm.
rows.anchor: وحكى النقاش عن مؤرج أنه قال: الإملاق الجوع بلغة لخم

rows.speaker: منذر بن سعيد
rows.claim: Mundhir ibn Sa'id says imlaq means spending, citing the verb for spending away one's property and a saying attributed to Ali.
rows.anchor: وذكر منذر بن سعيد أن الإملاق الإنفاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word malq can mean a flatterer who promises with his tongue what he does not hold in his heart, illustrating the root's range.
rows.anchor: ورجل ملق يعطي بلسانه ما ليس في قلبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some infer that coitus interruptus is forbidden by analogy to infanticide, since killing removes existing offspring while withdrawal prevents offspring at their origin; others say the Prophet's description of it as hidden infanticide signals dislike rather than prohibition.
rows.anchor: وقد يستدل بهذا من يمنع العزل لأن الوأد يرفع الموجود والنسل والعزل منع أصل النسل

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet called coitus interruptus hidden infanticide, a report used to argue against it.
rows.anchor: قوله عليه السلام في العزل: «ذلك الوأد الخفي»

rows.speaker: جماعة من الصحابة وغيرهم
rows.claim: A group of Companions, Successors, and jurists permit withdrawal, citing the Prophet's statement that there is no blame in refraining because destiny determines conception; Hasan and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna understood the report as discouraging it.
rows.anchor: لا عليكم ألا تفعلوا فإنما هو القدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi prefers permissibility as the first interpretation because nothing can prevent a child if God wills its creation.
rows.anchor:
والتأويل الأول أولى لقوله عليه السلام:
" وإذا أراد الله خلق شيء لم يمنعه شيء

rows.speaker: مالك والشافعي
rows.claim: Malik and al-Shafi'i require a free wife’s permission for withdrawal, viewing ejaculation as part of her pleasure and her right to children; they see no such right for a concubine.
rows.anchor: لا يجوز العزل عن الحرة إلا بإذنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All indecencies are prohibited, whether outward acts or inwardly held disobedience; outward and inward together exhaust the categories, and the phrase is grammatically appositional to al-fawahish.
rows.anchor: فقوله: «ما ظهر» نهي عن جميع أنواع الفواحش وهي المعاصي. «وما بطن» ما عقد عليه القلب من المخالفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The generic definite al-nafs parallels generic human statements qualified by exceptions; the verse forbids killing any protected life, Muslim or treaty-holder, except for a legally valid cause.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية نهي عن قتل النفس المحرمة، مؤمنة كانت أو معاهدة إلا بالحق

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says that anyone who testifies to God's oneness is protected in life and property, except by a rightful legal claim, and is answerable to God.
rows.anchor: فمن قال لا إله إلا الله فقد عصم ماله ونفسه إلا بحقه وحسابهم على الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Examples of a lawful cause include withholding zakat and abandoning prayer; Abu Bakr fought those who withheld zakat, and a Quranic verse orders release when people repent, pray, and give alms.
rows.anchor: وهذا الحق أمور: منها منع الزكاة وترك الصلاة وقد قاتل الصديق مانعي الزكاة
